\chapter{Review --- Three Joints, Two Constants}
\label{ch:repaso-reportar}
\hlchaptermodality{216}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can choose the right joint for anything I am reporting.}

I can choose the right joint for anything I am reporting.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[(review)]{(review)}

\label{lesson:ES-C57-repaso-reportar}



\begin{quote}
Two forms first, because the rest is built on them. \emph{He said.} (\emph{Dijo}.) \emph{They said.} (\emph{Dijeron} — no \emph{i}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Three chants. Say each one, then say what it is for.

\textbf{First.} \emph{Dijo que trabajaba.} — a statement goes in on \emph{\textbf{que}}, and \emph{que} may never be dropped.

\textbf{Second.} \emph{Preguntó si trabajaba.} — a yes-or-no question goes in on \emph{\textbf{si}}, the same \emph{si} that opens a condition.

\textbf{Third.} \emph{Preguntó dónde trabajaba.} — a question that starts with an asking word brings \textbf{its own joint}, accent and all.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the two things that never change}]
Whatever the joint, two things are true of all three chants.

\textbf{One.} The inner verb steps back into the imperfect — because a report says what was going on when somebody spoke.

\textbf{Two.} The question marks go. A report tells; it does not ask. And yet the accent on \emph{dónde} stays, because that accent was never marking the sentence — it marks the word that does the asking.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} the three chants, in order, without looking
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which tense does the inner verb land in, every time? (The \textbf{imperfect}.)

And one word to keep, for the pleasure of it: what is the \emph{j} of \emph{dijo}, historically? (A Latin \emph{\textbf{x}}. \emph{Dīxit}, \emph{dixo}, \emph{dijo}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
